On the following day the station graded 1,200 eggs, and the same proportion of them fell in the Large or Very Large classes. How many of the 1,200 eggs were graded Large or Very Large?
MATH_M1.check: 336 + 168 = 504 of the 800 eggs, or 63 percent, were Large or Very Large; 0.63(1,200) = 756.

MATH_M1.stem: The time needed to lift and empty the eel traps on a stretch of river is inversely proportional to the number of workers doing it. Six workers need 45 minutes. How many minutes would ten workers need?
MATH_M1.check: Inverse proportion means nt is constant, and 6(45) = 270, so ten workers need 270/10 = 27 minutes.

MATH_M1.stem:
Two graders each weighed five eggs, in grams, and recorded these results.
Grader P: 58, 60, 62, 64, 66
Grader Q: 52, 57, 62, 67, 72
Which statement correctly compares the two sets of five masses?
MATH_M1.check: Both sets total 310 grams, so both means are 62 grams. Grader P's masses lie within 4 grams of 62 while Grader Q's lie within 10 grams of 62, so Grader P's masses are less spread out and have the smaller standard deviation.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The two means are equal, and the standard deviation of Grader P's masses is less than the standard deviation of Grader Q's masses.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The two means are equal, and the standard deviation of Grader P's masses is greater than the standard deviation of Grader Q's masses.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The mean of Grader P's masses is greater, and the two standard deviations are equal.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The mean of Grader P's masses is less, and the standard deviation of Grader P's masses is greater.

MATH_M1.stem:
The table gives the number of eggs collected from a laying flock on each of six days.

On how many of these six days was the number of eggs collected greater than the mean number collected per day?
MATH_M1.check: The six counts total 1,684 eggs, so the mean is 1,684/6, about 280.7. The counts above that mean are 291, 302 and 285, which is three days.

MATH_M1.stem: A grading line handles 45 trays of eggs every 4 minutes, and each tray holds 30 eggs. At this rate, how many eggs pass along the line in one hour?
MATH_M1.check: 45/4 trays a minute is 675 trays an hour, and 675(30) = 20,250 eggs.

MATH_M1.stem: A weathering ground where hawks are put out on their blocks is a rectangle 14 metres long and 12 metres wide, with a semicircular bay of diameter 12 metres built out along one of the 12-metre sides. What is the total area of the weathering ground, in square metres?
MATH_M1.check: The rectangle has area 14(12) = 168 square metres. The bay is a semicircle of radius 6, with area (1/2)pi(6^2) = 18pi, so the total is 168 + 18pi.

MATH_M1.stem: In triangle ABC, the measure of angle A is 40° , and the measure of angle B is three times the measure of angle C. What is the measure, in degrees, of the exterior angle of the triangle at vertex B?
MATH_M1.check: Angles B and C sum to 140°, so 4C = 140, C = 35° and B = 105°; the exterior angle at B is 180 - 105 = 75°.

MATH_M1.stem: A falconer's flying lawn PQR is a triangle whose corner at R is a right angle. The side QR measures 60 metres, and \( \sin P = \frac{20}{29} \) . The lawn is to be fenced all the way round. How many metres of fencing are needed?
MATH_M1.check: sin P = QR/PQ = 20/29 with QR = 60 gives PQ = 87, and PR = sqrt(87^2 - 60^2) = sqrt(3969) = 63; the perimeter is 60 + 63 + 87 = 210.

MATH_M1.stem: An egg crate is a rectangular box measuring 60 centimetres by 40 centimetres by 30 centimetres on the inside. It is filled completely, with no space left over, by trays measuring 30 centimetres by 20 centimetres by 5 centimetres. Each tray holds 30 eggs. How many eggs does a full crate hold?
MATH_M1.check: The crate holds 60(40)(30) = 72,000 cubic centimetres and each tray occupies 30(20)(5) = 3,000, so 24 trays fit and 24(30) = 720 eggs.

MATH_M2E.stem: A pigeon loft has the same number of nest boxes in each of 5 rows, together with 18 further boxes on the end wall, and 63 nest boxes in all. How many nest boxes are in each row?
The number of squabs taken from a dovecote in its first m months of use is given by s = 24m + 15. How many squabs are taken in the first 6 months?
A loft keeper counting his birds writes 7n - 12 = 4n + 27, where n is the number of pigeons in the loft. What is the value of n?
MATH_M2E.check: Subtracting 4n from both sides gives 3n - 12 = 27, so 3n = 39 and n = 13.

MATH_M2E.stem: A tank used to carry carp from a stew pond has a total mass, in kilograms, given by M = 0.7n + 12, where n is the number of carp and 12 kilograms is the mass of the empty tank. What is the total mass when the tank holds 40 carp?
The number of pigeons n a loft may hold satisfies \( 3n+14 \le 71 \) . What is the greatest possible value of n?
MATH_M2E.check: 3n <= 57 gives n <= 19, so the greatest value is 19.

MATH_M2E.stem: A dovecote has three times as many nest holes on its upper tier as on its lower tier, and 96 nest holes in all. How many nest holes are on the upper tier?
MATH_M2E.check: With l on the lower tier, 3l + l = 96 gives l = 24, so the upper tier has 3(24) = 72.

MATH_M2E.stem: A wildfowler records the number of decoys d set out on a pond as more than 15 but no more than 40. Which inequality represents this?
MATH_M2E.check: 'More than 15' is a strict inequality at the lower end and 'no more than 40' allows 40, giving 15 < d <= 40.

MATH_M2E.stem: A dovecote's floor plan gives an area, in square metres, of \( (x+9)(x-4) \) , where x is a length in metres. Which expression is equivalent to that area?
A loft keeper's feed rule is modelled by the function h defined by \( h(x) = \frac{9}{x+6} \) . For what value of x is h(x) undefined?
MATH_M2E.check: A quotient is undefined only where its denominator is 0, and x + 6 = 0 when x = -6.

MATH_M2E.stem: The equation (x - 4)(x + 9) = 0 has two solutions. What is the sum of those two solutions?
Which expression is equivalent to 7a + 3b - 2a + 5b?
MATH_M2E.check: Collecting the a terms gives 7a - 2a = 5a and collecting the b terms gives 3b + 5b = 8b, so the expression is 5a + 8b.

MATH_M2E.stem:
The table gives four values of the linear function g.
x1234

What is the value of g(7)?
MATH_M2E.check: Each step of 1 in x raises g by 4, so g(x) = 4x + 3 and g(7) = 28 + 3 = 31.

MATH_M2E.stem: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 210. What is the greater of the two integers?
MATH_M2E.check: With n the smaller integer, n(n+1) = 210 gives n^2 + n - 210 = (n+15)(n-14) = 0, so the positive solution is n = 14 and the greater integer is 15.

MATH_M2E.stem: A decoy pond took 240 wildfowl in one season, and 35% of them were teal. How many teal were taken?
A dovecote yields 7 squabs a year from each nest hole. How many nest holes are needed to yield 245 squabs a year at that rate?
The masses, in kilograms, of five carp taken from a stew pond were 2.4, 3.1, 2.8, 3.6, and 3.1. What is the mean mass, in kilograms, of these five carp?
The numbers of wigeon counted flighting into a pond on five evenings were 23, 31, 18, 27, and 24. What is the median of these five counts?
MATH_M2E.check: In order the counts are 18, 23, 24, 27, 31, and the middle value is 24.

MATH_M2E.stem:
The table gives the numbers of teal and wigeon taken at a decoy pond in each of four months.
MonthTealWigeon

In November, how many more wigeon than teal were taken?
A stew pond is a rectangle measuring 18 metres by 25 metres. What is its area, in square metres?
Three of the four interior angles of a quadrilateral measure 95° , 128° , and 62° . What is the measure, in degrees, of the fourth interior angle?
MATH_M2E.check: The four interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360°, and 95 + 128 + 62 = 285, so the fourth angle measures 360 - 285 = 75°.

MATH_M2E.stem: A decoy pond is shaped like a trapezium whose two parallel sides measure 14 metres and 22 metres and whose perpendicular width is 9 metres. What is the area of the pond, in square metres?
MATH_M2E.check: The area of a trapezium is half the sum of the parallel sides times the perpendicular width, so it is (1/2)(14 + 22)(9) = 18(9) = 162 square metres.

MATH_M2E.stem: In right triangle ABC, the right angle is at vertex C, the hypotenuse AB has length 74, and \( \cos A = \frac{35}{37} \) . What is the length of side AC?
MATH_M2E.check: cos A is the side adjacent to A over the hypotenuse, that is AC/AB, so AC = 74(35/37) = 70.

MATH_M2H.stem: Two dovecotes yielded 148 squabs between them in one season. The larger dovecote yielded 16 more than twice as many squabs as the smaller. How many more squabs did the larger dovecote yield than the smaller?
MATH_M2H.check: With s squabs from the smaller dovecote the larger yielded 2s + 16, so s + 2s + 16 = 148 gives 3s = 132 and s = 44; the larger yielded 104, which is 60 more than 44.

MATH_M2H.stem: In the xy-plane, the line through the points (a, 3) and (7, 15) has slope 4. What is the y-coordinate of the point where this line crosses the y-axis?
MATH_M2H.check: (15-3)/(7-a) = 4 gives 7 - a = 3 and a = 4; then y = 4x + c through (7, 15) gives c = 15 - 28 = -13.

MATH_M2H.stem: What is the least integer value of x that satisfies \( -2 \lt 5-3x \le 11 \) ?
MATH_M2H.check: 5 - 3x <= 11 gives x >= -2, and -2 < 5 - 3x gives x < 7/3, so -2 <= x < 7/3 and the least integer is -2.

MATH_M2H.stem: At a decoy pond, 5 teal and 2 wigeon together weigh 4.3 kilograms, and 3 teal and 4 wigeon together weigh 4.4 kilograms. Every teal weighs the same as every other teal, and every wigeon the same as every other wigeon. What is the mass, in grams, of one wigeon?
MATH_M2H.check: Doubling the first equation gives 10t + 4w = 8.6; subtracting 3t + 4w = 4.4 gives 7t = 4.2, so t = 0.6 kilograms and w = (4.4 - 1.8)/4 = 0.65 kilograms, or 650 grams.

MATH_M2H.stem: The mass of feed a pigeon loft consumes in a week is modelled by \( M = \frac{kn}{n+c} \) , where n is the number of birds in the loft and k and c are positive constants with M less than k. Which expression gives n in terms of M, k and c?
MATH_M2H.check: M(n+c) = kn gives Mn + Mc = kn, so n(k - M) = Mc and n = Mc/(k - M).

MATH_M2H.stem: A wildfowler sets x teal decoys and y wigeon decoys on a pond. The pond takes no more than 60 decoys altogether, and she always sets at least twice as many teal decoys as wigeon decoys. Which ordered pair (x, y) satisfies both of these conditions?

MATH_M2H.stem: What value of x satisfies \( \frac{x}{4} + \frac{x}{6} = \frac{x-14}{2} \) ?
MATH_M2H.check: Multiplying through by 12 gives 3x + 2x = 6(x - 14), so 5x = 6x - 84 and x = 84.

MATH_M2H.stem: For a constant k, \( (3x+k)^{2} = 9x^{2}+42x+c \) for every value of x, where c is a constant. What is the value of c?
MATH_M2H.check: Expanding gives 9x^2 + 6kx + k^2, so 6k = 42 and k = 7, and c = k^2 = 49.

MATH_M2H.stem: One solution to the equation \( 2x^{2}+kx-30=0 \) is x = 5, where k is a constant. What is the other solution to that equation?
MATH_M2H.check: Substituting x = 5 gives 50 + 5k - 30 = 0, so k = -4 and the equation is 2x^2 - 4x - 30 = 0, that is x^2 - 2x - 15 = (x-5)(x+3) = 0; the other solution is x = -3.

MATH_M2H.stem: In the equation \( 2(x-3)^{3} = 54 \) , what is the value of x?
MATH_M2H.check: Dividing by 2 gives (x-3)^3 = 27, so x - 3 = 3 and x = 6.

MATH_M2H.stem: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = ax + 3 and g(x) = x + a, where a is a positive constant. If f(g(2)) = 18, what is the value of a?
MATH_M2H.check: g(2) = 2 + a, so f(g(2)) = a(2+a) + 3 = a^2 + 2a + 3 = 18, giving a^2 + 2a - 15 = 0 and a = 3 or a = -5; only a = 3 is positive.

MATH_M2H.stem: Which single fraction is equal to \( \frac{5}{x^{2}-4} - \frac{1}{x-2} \) , where \( x \gt 2 \) ?
MATH_M2H.check: Factoring the first denominator as (x-2)(x+2) shows the common denominator is x^2 - 4, over which the numerator is 5 - (x+2) = 3 - x.

MATH_M2H.stem: The function f is defined by \( f(x) = x^{2}+3x \) . What is the average rate of change of f from x = 2 to x = 5?
MATH_M2H.check: f(2) = 4 + 6 = 10 and f(5) = 25 + 15 = 40, so the average rate of change is (40 - 10)/(5 - 2) = 30/3 = 10.

MATH_M2H.stem: A stew pond can be emptied by a large pipe alone in 6 hours or by a small pipe alone in 9 hours. Both pipes are opened together, and after 2 hours the large pipe is shut. How many more hours does the small pipe need to finish emptying the pond?
MATH_M2H.check: In 2 hours the two pipes empty 2(1/6 + 1/9) = 5/9 of the pond, leaving 4/9; the small pipe empties 1/9 of the pond an hour, so it needs 4 more hours.

MATH_M2H.stem: A rectangular tank measuring 60 centimetres by 40 centimetres holds water to a depth of 15 centimetres. A basket of carp is lowered in and sinks completely, raising the water to a depth of 22 centimetres. Given that 1 litre is 1,000 cubic centimetres, what is the volume, in litres, of the basket and its carp together?
MATH_M2H.check: The water rises 22 - 15 = 7 centimetres over a base of 60(40) = 2,400 square centimetres, so the basket and carp displace 2,400(7) = 16,800 cubic centimetres, which is 16.8 litres.

MATH_M2H.stem: The floor of a dovecote is a regular polygon, and each of its interior angles measures 156° . How many sides does the polygon have?
MATH_M2H.check: Each exterior angle measures 180 - 156 = 24°, and the exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360°, so the polygon has 360/24 = 15 sides.

MATH_M2H.stem: In right triangle JKL, the right angle is at vertex L. The leg KL has length 33, and \( \tan J = \frac{33}{56} \) . What is the length of JK?
MATH_M2H.check: tan J is the side opposite J over the side adjacent to J, that is KL/JL, so JL = 56. JK is the hypotenuse, and sqrt(33^2 + 56^2) = sqrt(4225) = 65.

MATH_M2H.stem: Two conical feed hoppers are similar in shape, and their heights are in the ratio 2 to 5. The smaller hopper holds 96 litres. How many litres does the larger hopper hold?
MATH_M2H.check: Volumes of similar solids scale as the cube of the ratio, so the larger holds 96(5/2)^3 = 96(125/8) = 1,500 litres.
